Hi Jill — thanks for the note and great question. Short answer: we can support both approaches and will work to match what your AP prefers. Below are two common options we’ve handled for committed (reserved) spend: 

1) Single upfront invoice (annual prepay): Redwood issues one invoice at contract start for the committed amount. That invoice is applied as a prepaid credit; consumption is reconciled monthly against that credit. This reduces invoicing overhead for both sides.

2) Split/drawdown invoicing: Redwood issues an initial invoice for a portion (e.g., 30–50%) to secure capacity, then issues periodic drawdown invoices (monthly or quarterly) for consumption or scheduled slices of the committed amount. Each drawdown invoice references the master agreement and the remaining committed balance.

For Acme we can do either. Attached is a short PDF showing the two sample invoice layouts and a CSV template we use for monthly drawdown statements so your AP can import it into your ledger. If you prefer one approach, tell me which cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and whether you need the annual invoice to say “Tax excluded / Tax to be applied by vendor.”

Next steps I suggest:
- You confirm preferred cadence and whether Acme needs separate drawdown invoices or a single annual invoice + monthly statements.
- If you want W-9 or Redwood tax details I’ll loop in finance to share the official documents.

I’m looping Rafael (ACM) to keep the account team in the loop.

Best,

Thanks for the ping — quick answers and suggested playbook below.

Short answers: for US customers we do not charge VAT; we provide a W-9 and Redwood’s EIN for vendor setup. For EU customers we provide a VAT registration number and apply VAT where required.

Recommended playbook for Acme (US entity):
A) Preferred (low overhead): Single annual prepay invoice for the committed amount. We’ll apply the payment as a prepaid credit on their account and send monthly consumption statements (CSV) that show the remaining committed balance. No further invoicing unless they request replenishment.

B) If Acme prefers periodic invoicing: Initial invoice to secure the commitment (30–50% typical), followed by monthly drawdown invoices that reference the master agreement and remaining committed balance. Our AP team can generate a monthly statement CSV and a short PDF invoice for each drawdown.

Required docs we can attach: W-9 (we’ll provide the signed PDF), sample drawdown invoice PDF, and the CSV template for your ledger import (attached).
